cells.tense: Right now you're inside this choosing, and your hand is on it — what's coming toward you is being met cleanly, on purpose, not just let in.
cells.ask: let the direction that's forming now pick up your own momentum — and notice how much further it carries when you're the one pushing it.
cells.sheetLine: You're walking into something real and steering it yourself.
cells.core:
What's arriving is landing well and you're the one deciding to let it. That's rarer than it sounds. Plenty of people meet a real connection and stall at the door — you're already through it and walking together.

The steadiness you've got here isn't built yet, and it doesn't need to be. Engagement itself is the fuel: the more genuinely you're in it, the more the direction shows up on its own. You don't have to manufacture the next step or prove the thing is real before you move. Let the next thing that stirs you be the thing you steer by. Choosing with your feet is enough, and it's the part that keeps holding when the feeling wavers.

cells.tense: You're already living in what this might become — leaning past what's actually here toward a version that hasn't arrived, bracing for it before it's yours to carry.
cells.ask: let the thing you're tending show you when it's ready — reach for the result only as fast as your care has actually grown it.
cells.core:
When the contact is good, it's easy — the meeting happens and you move with it. What you're doing now is different. You're at the gate working the relationship before it's begun, running the next steps ahead of the ones you're in. The leaning itself is what's costing you the entrance.

What's arriving doesn't need you to hurry it. Tending something and then stepping back to watch it grow is its own kind of action — the harvest comes from the care you gave. Hold what's here loosely enough that it can put down roots. You can't force a thing into being ready.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping what hasn't arrived yet, and it's costing you what has.

cells.tense: You're still standing where something already came in — the door's behind you and you're facing it, not the room you've already entered.
cells.ask: put one real question in front of someone you trust and let their answer stand on its own — you don't have to already know before you can reach.
cells.core:
In a good week, what comes in gets recognized — you feel something arriving and you move toward it. What's happened here is harder to name. Something genuine came toward you and you're not reaching for it. Not because you can't; because you've settled into watching the door instead of walking from it.

The knowing that makes connection possible doesn't need you to be certain first. You can put a question out into the room and let the answer carry itself. The moment you trust a perception without needing to test it twice, the door opens from your side. Nothing else is required for the entrance to happen.
cells.sheetLine: Something's already entered, and you're watching the door instead of it.

cells.tense: You're in the middle of this choosing even now — the hand that makes it is yours, but you're not counting it as yours.
cells.ask: start with one small practice, daily and plain — a minute of stillness before you decide anything — and let it show you the line you're already walking.
cells.core:
You meet things and you move with them — connection forms around you in how you listen, what you notice, who you follow. Good. The meeting is real. What's missing is the one saying so.

The choosing is already happening; you just haven't called it a choice. Come back to something simpler than the whole thing: one small daily act, done plainly, that keeps you pointed at where you're headed. When the practice is steady, the direction tends itself. Nothing needs to be forced or performed. Just let the quiet fact of your own hand become something you can say out loud.
cells.sheetLine: You're choosing this already — you just haven't put your name on it.
